title: Universal derived quotient towers with their ordinary-unit normalization
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $q_n:R\to S_n$ a compatible inverse sequence of ring-sheaf maps with transitions $t_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n$. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on these maps. Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ for strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system]. Define the additive module functor $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal T$ by $T(M)_n=\operatorname{Res}_{q_n}(S_n\otimes_R M)$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Its transitions send $s\otimes m$ to $t_n(s)\otimes m$, and its augmentation $\eta:\Delta\to T$ sends $m$ to $1\otimes m$. These are the sheafified pure-tensor maps, natural and compatible with every transition. Let $T^c,T^h$ be its termwise cochain and homotopy functors, and $Q^h,Q^h_{\mathcal T}$ the unbounded derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
The functor $T^c$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat $R$-complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], without a flat-term assumption. There exists $LT:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal T)$ with a counit $\epsilon:LTQ^h\to Q^h_{\mathcal T}T^h$ which is a universal right Kan extension along $Q^h$: for every $G$ and $a:GQ^h\to Q^h_{\mathcal T}T^h$ there is a unique $b:G\to LT$ with $\epsilon(bQ^h)=a$. For every K-flat cochain complex $P$, $\epsilon_{pP}$ is invertible, where $p$ is quotient by chain homotopy. Every complex has a K-flat resolution on which these computations apply. The ordinary augmentation remains the specified $1\otimes m$ map; no derived completion unit is included in this assertion.

source.place: Tag 099M (proetale-lemma-naive-completion): strict reduction functor, its scalar-unit augmentation and universal K-flat homotopy presentation; categorical construction written by the worker

proof.text: Put $\Delta M=(M\xleftarrow{1}M\xleftarrow{1}\cdots)$. On sections define $T(a)_n(s\otimes m)=s\otimes a(m)$ and $\tau_n(s\otimes m)=t_n(s)\otimes m$. Compatibility $t_nq_{n+1}=q_n$ makes $\tau_n$ balanced over $R$ and $R$-linear; both formulas commute with restrictions and hence sheafify. The identities $T(ba)=T(b)T(a)$, $T(1)=1$, $T(a+b)=T(a)+T(b)$, and $\tau_nT(a)_{n+1}=T(a)_n\tau_n$ hold on pure tensors and therefore after sheafification. Thus these formulas define an additive strict-tower functor. The maps $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ are $R$-linear, commute with restrictions and module maps, and satisfy $\tau_n(1\otimes m)=t_n(1)\otimes m=1\otimes m$; they give exactly the specified natural augmentation $\eta:\Delta\to T$.

source.place: Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), reduction tower; elementary sectionwise construction of its ordinary scalar-unit augmentation

proof.text: Kernels of strict-tower maps are the component kernels, with transitions restricted to them; cokernels are the component cokernels, with the induced transitions. Their universal maps assemble uniquely because the component maps commute with transitions. The abelian identities are therefore checked at each level, so $\mathcal T$ is abelian and $H^i(X)_n=H^i(X_n)$. A tower map is an isomorphism if and only if every component is: naturality for the component inverses follows by multiplying the original naturality equation by those inverses. Consequently quasi-isomorphisms of tower complexes are exactly componentwise quasi-isomorphisms. Restriction of scalars keeps the underlying abelian sheaf, sectionwise kernels and sheafified cokernels, so it keeps cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms.

Let a:P→P′ be a quasi-isomorphism with both complexes K-flat. For every n, apply the proved independent-coefficient K-flat invariance helper derivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients_kflat_invariance from the generic ringed-site implementation of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to q_n and the ordinary scalar-extension functor. This is the arbitrary-universe version of the originally cited change-of-rings K-flat invariance step; it imposes no flat-term condition. Restriction to R preserves the underlying abelian sheaf, hence preserves quasi-isomorphisms by exact faithful forgetting to abelian sheaves. The componentwise criterion of Step 2 then shows T^c(a) is a quasi-isomorphism. Neither surjectivity nor flatness of q_n is used.

source.place: Tag 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side), specialization to S_n in degree zero, and Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change)

proof.text: Apply $T$ to differentials and to a homotopy equation $a-b=dh+hd$; additivity preserves that equation, yielding $T^h:K(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathcal T)$. It also gives $T(P[1])\cong T(P)[1]$ and $T(C(a))\cong C(T(a))$: the canonical biproduct comparison identifies the cone differential with the matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}T(d)&T(a)\\0&-T(d)\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, and identifies its inclusion and negative projection. Hence $F=Q^h_{\mathcal T}T^h$ sends the standard cone triangles to distinguished triangles and is exact. This uses only the cone and shift formulas for the homotopy and derived categories, not exactness of the module functor $T$.

source.place: Cone and distinguished-triangle formulas (definition-cone and definition-distinguished-triangle); elementary matrix calculation

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the class of all K-flat complexes, with no condition on their terms. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], each complex $X$ has a quasi-isomorphism $P\to X$ with $P\in\mathcal P$ (indeed $P$ can also have flat terms). Step 3 shows that $F$ inverts every quasi-isomorphism between objects of $\mathcal P$, since $Q^h_{\mathcal T}$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The two hypotheses of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] now hold for the exact functor $F$ of Step 4. Its conclusion gives $LT:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal T)$ and $\epsilon:LTQ^h\to F$, universal among such pairs, with $\epsilon_{pP}$ invertible for every $P\in\mathcal P$. Expanding that universal property gives the unique $b:G\to LT$ satisfying $\epsilon(bQ^h)=a$ for every $a:GQ^h\to F$. The augmentation retained is the ordinary transformation constructed in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual assertion; Tag 05S9 and equation-everywhere (universal property); resolutions: sites-cohomology Tag 06YS

proof_origin.place: Assembly of Tags 06YT and 06YS with derived.tex Tag 06XN; the K-flat invariance step uses the already proved independent-coefficient helper in Sheaf.Algebra.Homology.DerivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients. The ordinary strict tower and scalar-unit augmentation are constructed sectionwise and extended through the locally bijective sheafification unit. Tag 099M supplies context, not the general ring-map theorem.
